name: Liquid Chrome
rationale: Clean-room WebGL port written from the one-line effect description only (no upstream source read): a dependency-free fragment shader turns hero panels and cards into flowing mirror-polished metal that can react to the pointer, with a banded CSS chrome gradient when WebGL is unavailable.

tint.description: Metal tint, as #rgb or #rrggbb; also tints the CSS fallback gradient.

speed.description: Flow speed; 0 holds a still frame.

amplitude.description: Warp strength: how far the surface folds.

frequency.description: Ripple density; larger gives more, smaller ripples.

interactive.description: Let the pointer press a soft dent into the flow; it never intercepts clicks or focus.

a11y: The injected canvas is aria-hidden and pointer-events: none; the host's content, reading order and focus behaviour are unchanged, and pointer tracking is passive and never captures clicks.
Chrome swings between near-white highlights and near-black bands, so text must sit on its own scrim to keep 4.5:1 contrast (the demo uses a dark panel).
Reduced motion stops the shader loop, the pointer easing and the fallback drift, and shows one still frame of the metal.
Forced-colors mode hides the canvas and paints the host in Canvas/CanvasText with a visible border.
